model_annotation: The chart illustrates measured “effect” values across language families, with multiple model variants shown as grouped bars for each family. The horizontal axis contains the categorical variable “family,” ordered left to right as IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear scale with labeled ticks at 0, 10, 20, and 30 (values extending slightly above 30), and each bar includes vertical error bars indicating uncertainty. For each family, six adjacent bars appear in the legend order: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). In IE-Baltic, the bars are small, roughly around 1–6 (light blue ≈2, dark blue ≈1, light green ≈3, dark green ≈3, pink ≈6, red ≈5). In IE-Germanic, light and dark blue are around 9–10, the green bars are near 0 with one slightly negative, and the pink and red bars are around 15. In IE-Indic, the blue bars are near 0, the green bars are high (light green ≈20 and dark green ≈18), and the pink and red bars are higher still (pink ≈24 and red ≈21). In IE-Romance, light blue is around 6, dark blue around 4, light green around 5, dark green around 1, pink around 12–13, and red around 6. In IE-Slavic, light blue is around 10–11, dark blue around 9, the green bars are near 0–1, and the pink and red bars are around 17 and 15–16, respectively. In IE-other, the blue bars are around 6, the green bars are near 0 (one slightly negative), and the pink and red bars are around 8. In Isolate, all bars cluster close to 0–2 with small error bars. In Semitic, light blue is around 11, dark blue around 16, the green bars are slightly negative (around −2 to −1), and the pink and red bars are around 15 and about 19–20, with the red bar showing the largest error range in the figure. In Uralic, all bars are near 0–2 with small error bars. The bars are not sorted by height; they are grouped by family with consistent within-group color ordering, and no bars appear specially emphasized beyond the error bars.
